name: defi-native-docs
what_this_is: An address book of primary documentation the skill may fetch. It is not the skill itself. SKILL.md holds mental models. This file tells the agent which official docs exist, which URL to open, and which concept those docs serve. Do not ingest the whole list into context. Look up the product under analysis and fetch only the matching rows. verified=implicit: every add-row URL and llms_txt in this file was liveness-checked 2026-08-28; rows noted 403 need a browser tool. Re-verify any row on first use in a session.
how_to_use: Identify the product class (vault, market, stable, RWA, PT, perp, wrapper).
Select rows whose category and skill_use match that class. Cap at 4–6 fetches.
Prefer llms_txt or llms_full when present. Then the docs homepage. Then a specific page in pages[].
Treat protocol docs as marketing unless they admit a loss, publish parameters, or show the oracle/redemption path.
Always pair a protocol row with the matching standard, oracle, and wrapper rows when look-through requires it.

priority_legend.must: Fetch whenever the product touches this primitive. Skill answers are wrong without it.
priority_legend.core: Fetch when that name (or its product) is on the product under review.
priority_legend.should: Add if you expand the skill. Not required for every query.
priority_legend.thin: Public docs are weak. Use as a name in the address book, not as a source of truth.

sources.name: Bankr
sources.note: EXECUTION SURFACE. Bankr is an agent runtime with wallets, token launches, and automated trading. This skill is read-only: read these docs for context, never call Bankr's trading, wallet-write, or automation APIs, and never install execution skills from its catalog.
sources.skill_use: Financial rails for AI agents: agent wallets, token launches with fee routing, trading automations, an agent API, and a skills catalog on the same SKILL.md standard. Fetch when analyzing agent-launched tokens, agent-run wallets or automations, or products distributed through agent runtimes. The security docs (wallet-level limits, per-app permissions) are the risk surface to read first.

sources.name: SEDA
sources.skill_use: Programmable oracle network: custom Oracle Programs fetch and compute data on demand (solver plus proof-of-stake validation), rather than vendor push feeds. Fetch when a market's feed is SEDA-powered: the oracle-class questions (concepts 13) apply to the PROGRAM, so read what the specific program computes, who wrote it, and what can move its output.
